content: 1. The use of a moderate CYP2C9 inducer in combination with a moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducer is not recommended. 2. Co-administration of moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers alone is not recommended for patients with CYP2C9 1/3 and 2/3 genotypes. 3. Rifapentine reduces sirolimus levels or effects by altering hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 4. Rifapentine decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Co-administration with antibiotics reduces the efficacy of sodium picosulfate by altering colonic bacterial flora required for its activation. Use alternative therapy. 6. Rifapentine reduces sofosbuvir levels or effects by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. P-gp inducers decrease sofosbuvir levels, reducing its conversion to the active metabolite GS-331007, which accounts for 90% of its pharmacologic effect. 8. Rifapentine reduces sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels or effects by altering hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Velpatasvir is metabolized by CYP2B6, CYP2C8, and CYP3A4. Moderate-to-potent inducers of these enzymes may significantly reduce velpatasvir plasma concentrations, potentially diminishing its therapeutic effect. 10. Rifapentine reduces solifenacin levels or effects by altering hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Rifapentine reduces sonidegib levels or effects by altering hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Avoid co-administration of sonidegib with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 13. Rifapentine reduces sorafenib levels by increasing its metabolism. Use alternative therapy. 14. Rifapentine reduces sotrasib levels or effects by altering hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Rifapentine reduces stiripentol levels or effects by altering hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, increase the stiripentol dose. 16. Rifapentine reduces sufentanil levels or effects by altering hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 17. Co-administration of CYP3A4 inducers may decrease sufentanil levels and efficacy, potentially causing withdrawal syndrome in physically dependent patients. Discontinuation of the inducer may increase sufentanil plasma concentration. 18. Rifapentine reduces sulfamethoxazole levels or effects by altering hepatic CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitor closely. 19. Rifapentine reduces sunitinib levels or effects by altering hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Rifapentine reduces suvorexant levels or effects by altering hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Strong CYP3A4 inducers may decrease suvorexant efficacy. If an increased dose is required, do not exceed 20 mg/day. 22. Rifapentine reduces tacrolimus levels or effects by altering hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Rifapentine reduces tadalafil levels or effects by altering hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid combination in pulmonary hypertension patients. For erectile dysfunction patients, monitor response carefully due to potential reduced effectiveness. 24.
